items.prompt: A plain dict contains A then B. Its value for A is reassigned. Does that alone implement this cache's refresh rule?

options.text: Yes, reassignment automatically moves A after B.
options.why: An existing dict key keeps its insertion position on value reassignment.

options.text: Yes, because values determine recency order.
options.why: Recency is an explicit state transition, not a sort by values.

options.text: No, because dictionaries cannot update existing values.
options.why: They can update values; insertion order is the missing behavior.

options.text: No, the task also requires explicitly moving A to MRU.
options.why: OrderedDict.move_to_end supplies the required order change after assigning the value.

items.explanation: OrderedDict.move_to_end supplies the required order change after assigning the value.
